ZZCOLLAB Configuration System

ZZCOLLAB Development Team

2026-10-19

Source: vignettes/configuration.Rmd
configuration.Rmd

Overview

ZZCOLLAB’s configuration system controls which Docker image a project builds on, which rendering capabilities (PDF, Quarto) it carries, and a handful of developer-experience toggles (language server, linting). This vignette describes what the two-file configuration hierarchy actually does, verified against the current shell implementation (modules/config.sh, modules/docker.sh), not against an aspirational design. Where something documented in earlier versions of this guide turned out not to exist in the code, it has been removed rather than carried forward; those removals are called out explicitly in Section 8.

For a mechanical, line-by-line account of exactly how each setting reaches the generated Dockerfile — including the one genuinely non-trivial interaction, between the pdf and archetype settings — see docs/dockerfile-variable-reference.md in the package source. This vignette is the user-facing summary of the decisions that matter; that document is the reference for the mechanics behind them.

Key terms in this vignette. New to the vocabulary? These are the terms this guide uses; each is defined again on first use. Full definitions are in vignette('glossary').

  • Profile: the Docker image bundle the environment is built from (minimal, tidyverse, rstudio, publishing; analysis is a deprecated alias for tidyverse as a profile name — see the warning in Section 4 about the unrelated analysis archetype).
  • Archetype: the research-compendium shape a project scaffolds (analysis, manuscript, book, blog, package, simulation). Two archetypes (manuscript, book) default the project to needing a PDF toolchain; see Section 5.
  • Capability (pdf): an explicit, tri-state override (true/false/unset) for whether the Dockerfile installs a TeX Live toolchain, independent of archetype.
  • Two-layer package management: shared, image-baked packages (Layer 1) versus per-user packages added at runtime (Layer 2).
  • Base image: the starting Docker image a project builds on (e.g. rocker/tidyverse, rocker/verse).
  • Team image: a pre-built Docker image shared via a registry so every collaborator works from a byte-identical environment.
  • zzc / zzcollab: the framework’s command-line interface; zzc is an alias for zzcollab.

Key Features

  • Two-layer configuration: user config (~/.zzcollab/config.yaml) and project config (./zzcollab.yaml), merged with project values winning. There is no system-wide (/etc/zzcollab/...) configuration layer despite a constant of that name existing in the source — see Section 8.
  • Docker profile system: four built-in profiles (minimal, tidyverse, rstudio, publishing); other base images are reached with --base/--base-image, not through additional named profiles.
  • Capability gating: pdf (TeX Live + Quarto) is resolved per project from explicit config, remembered state, or archetype default — not hardcoded to a profile.
  • Two-layer package architecture: Docker image (team/shared) + renv (personal/flexible).
  • CLI and R interfaces: most configuration is set via the zzc/ zzcollab CLI; a narrower R interface wraps the same commands.

Configuration Philosophy

Set defaults once (zzc config set ...), override per project (zzc config set-local ... or editing ./zzcollab.yaml directly), and let zzc docker/zzc rebuild regenerate the Dockerfile from whatever the merged configuration says — a project’s Dockerfile is not something fixed once at zzc init time; it is regenerated from current settings every time the docker-generation path runs.

Configuration Hierarchy

Priority Order (Highest to Lowest)

Verified against load_config() in modules/config.sh:

  1. Project config — ./zzcollab.yaml, loaded last and so winning over user config for any key it sets.
  2. User config — ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml, loaded first.
  3. Built-in shell defaults — hardcoded fallbacks in the relevant module (e.g. languageserver defaults to true, docker_runtime to docker, ZZCOLLAB_DEFAULT_R_VERSION to 4.6.0).

A handful of CLI flags (--profile, --base/--base-image, --r-version, --no-renv) and a handful of specific environment variables (PPM_SNAPSHOT, ZZCOLLAB_QUARTO_VERSION, ZZRENVCHECK_TAG) sit above all of this when supplied — they are read directly by the generation code, not merged through load_config(). But there is no generic environment-variable override layer for ordinary config keys: setting a ZZCOLLAB_TEAM_NAME environment variable, for instance, has no effect. If you want a setting changed for one invocation only, pass the CLI flag (if one exists) or edit ./zzcollab.yaml temporarily; there is no third way.

There is also no system-wide configuration file. lib/constants.sh defines ZZCOLLAB_CONFIG_SYSTEM="/etc/zzcollab/config.yaml", but load_config() never reads it — it loads only $CONFIG_USER and $CONFIG_PROJECT. An organization wanting shared defaults across many users today has to distribute a project-config template, not an /etc file. See Section 8.

Configuration Locations

User Configuration (~/.zzcollab/config.yaml)

Personal defaults across all your projects:

# ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml
defaults:
  team_name: "myteam"
  github_account: "myusername"
  dockerhub_account: "myusername"
  profile_name: "tidyverse"
  languageserver: true

When to use: set your personal preferences once; every new project inherits them unless the project config overrides a key.

Project Configuration (./zzcollab.yaml)

Project-specific overrides, intended to be committed:

# ./zzcollab.yaml (in project root)
defaults:
  profile_name: "tidyverse"
  archetype: "manuscript"
  pdf: "true"

When to use: pin a project’s profile, archetype, or capability settings so zzc docker/zzc rebuild reproduces the same Dockerfile regardless of who runs it or what their personal user config says. This is also what zzc config set-local KEY VALUE writes to.

A real example, generated by zzc config set-local pdf true on a tidyverse-profile blog post that needed PDF output without switching archetype:

# Project-specific zzcollab configuration
# Overrides user config (~/.zzcollab/config.yaml)
# Commit this file to version control.
defaults:
  pdf: "true"

CLI Configuration Commands

Essential Configuration Commands

Initialize Configuration 

# Create the user configuration file (interactive prompts for
# team_name, github_account, profile_name)
zzc config init

# Same, explicitly interactive (default is already interactive when no
# config file exists)
zzc config init --interactive

Set Configuration Values 

# Set team name
zzc config set team-name "myteam"

# Set GitHub account
zzc config set github-account "myusername"

# Set Docker Hub account
zzc config set dockerhub-account "myusername"

# Set the default Docker profile
zzc config set profile-name "tidyverse"

# Set the default archetype for new projects
zzc config set archetype "manuscript"

# Declare whether this project/user needs a PDF toolchain
zzc config set pdf "true"

# Opt out of the in-container R language server (default: true)
zzc config set languageserver false

# Pre-select 'create remote now' in the init feature wizard (default: false)
zzc config set auto_github true

CLI keys are kebab-case (profile-name, dockerhub-account) and are normalized to the snake_case form used internally (profile_name, dockerhub_account) before being written — either spelling is accepted on the command line.

zzc config set validates several keys against a fixed value set and rejects anything else with an error naming the valid values:

Key Valid values
profile_name / profile minimal, tidyverse, analysis (deprecated alias for tidyverse), rstudio, publishing
archetype manuscript, analysis, book, package, simulation, blog
docker_runtime docker, podman, apptainer
validate_strict, validate_fix, auto_github, languageserver, remote_allow true, false
forge github, gitlab, none

languageserver (default true) installs the R language server in the Docker image so an editor gets in-container LSP completion and diagnostics. zzcollab assumes no R on the host, so the language server must run in the container; a host editor (vim, VS Code) bridges its LSP client into the container. Set languageserver false for REPL-only workflows.

auto_github (default false), when true, pre-selects the ‘create remote now’ checkbox in the init feature wizard so the compendium’s GitHub remote is created during initialization.

pdf (tri-state: true/false/unset) declares whether the project needs a PDF rendering toolchain. See Section 5 for how this interacts with archetype and with the base image’s existing capabilities — it is the one setting in this system with real cross-variable logic behind it, and the one most worth understanding before setting blindly.

A name collides with itself. analysis is simultaneously a valid value for archetype (a plain data-analysis compendium, the default archetype) and a deprecated value for profile_name (an old name for the tidyverse Docker profile, kept only for backward compatibility). Setting archetype: analysis and setting profile_name: analysis do completely different, unrelated things. This is a real naming collision in the current code, not a typo in this document.

Get Configuration Values 

zzc config get team-name
# Output: myteam

zzc config get profile-name
# Output: tidyverse  (or whatever the merged user+project config says)

config get reads the merged (project-overrides-user) value for a single key; it does not report which file the value came from.

List All Configuration 

# Show the full merged configuration (sections: author, license,
# r_package, style, plus team/profile/archetype/pdf/docker settings)
zzc config list

# Show only the project-local config file's own contents
zzc config list --local

There is no --verbose flag on config list, and the output does not annotate which file supplied each value — if you need to know whether a value is coming from user config or project config, the only way is to inspect ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml and ./zzcollab.yaml directly, or run config list --local to see the project file’s own content in isolation and compare.

Validate Configuration 

zzc config validate

This checks that ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml and ./zzcollab.yaml (if present) each parse as valid YAML via yq eval '.'. It does not check cross-key consistency, does not check that a referenced profile exists, and produces plain Valid YAML: <path> / Malformed YAML: <path> lines rather than a checklist — there is no --verbose mode and no “configuration hierarchy is consistent” check.

Configuration Workflow Examples

Solo Researcher Setup 

zzc config init
zzc config set team-name "myresearch"
zzc config set github-account "myusername"
zzc config set profile-name "tidyverse"

# Create projects using the configured defaults
mkdir penguin-study && cd penguin-study
zzc tidyverse          # init + renv + docker, using the resolved profile

Team Lead Setup 

zzc config set team-name "genomicslab"
zzc config set github-account "genomicslab"
zzc config set profile-name "tidyverse"

mkdir cancer-study && cd cancer-study
zzc tidyverse
zzc github             # create private GitHub repo

# Pin the profile for the project explicitly, independent of whatever
# collaborators have set in their own user config
zzc config set-local profile-name "tidyverse"

make docker-build
make docker-push-team
git add . && git commit -m "Initial team setup" && git push

Team Member Setup 

zzc config set team-name "genomicslab"

git clone https://github.com/genomicslab/cancer-study.git
cd cancer-study
make docker-build       # builds from the committed Dockerfile

# ./zzcollab.yaml (committed) supplies the project's profile/archetype/
# pdf settings; only account identity needs to come from user config

CLI Flags Reference

Project Initialization 

mkdir study1 && cd study1
zzc tidyverse           # full setup: init + renv + docker, tidyverse profile
zzc github              # create private GitHub repo
zzc config set dockerhub-account myteam
# Image name becomes: myteam/<project>:latest

Docker Profile Selection 

zzc minimal             # ~650MB, essential dev tools, rocker/r-ver
zzc tidyverse           # ~1.2GB, tidyverse ecosystem, rocker/tidyverse
zzc rstudio             # ~980MB, RStudio Server, rocker/rstudio
zzc publishing          # ~4.2GB, manuscript rendering, rocker/verse

# For Shiny, Bioconductor, geospatial, or other domains: build on a
# custom base image and add packages via renv
zzc docker --base rocker/shiny

zzc list profiles       # list profiles with base images and sizes
zzc list libs           # list system library bundles
zzc list pkgs           # list R package bundles

Custom Docker Composition 

zzc docker --base rocker/r-ver:latest
zzc docker --base rocker/rstudio:4.3.0
zzc docker --base bioconductor/bioconductor_docker:latest

--base accepts any syntactically valid Docker image reference (validate_base_image() checks the string format only; it does not check the image against a known list). Additional R packages are installed inside the container and captured in renv.lock — the package set lives there, not in a CLI flag. System library dependencies needed by those packages are derived automatically from code + DESCRIPTION + renv.lock, filtered against what the chosen base already ships.

Switching Profile on an Existing Project 

zzc docker --profile minimal     # regenerate Dockerfile for a different
                                  # profile; non-destructive

This is the command used to move a project from, say, tidyverse to minimal without recreating it — exactly the kind of change this vignette’s companion reference document (dockerfile-variable- reference.md) walks through the consequences of, including the package-list reproducibility gap that a profile switch can expose: a project whose code relies on packages the old base image happened to ship, but which are declared nowhere in renv.lock/DESCRIPTION, will fail to find them after switching to a leaner base. Check what your code actually library()s against what renv.lock actually pins before switching down to a smaller profile.

Output and Behavior Flags 

zzc -v docker            # -v / --verbose : detailed output
zzc -q config list       # -q / --quiet : errors only
zzc -y tidyverse         # -y / --yes (-Y / --yes-all) : accept defaults
zzc --no-build docker    # skip the Docker build prompt

Docker Profile System

Understanding Docker Profiles

A profile resolves to exactly one thing in the generator: a base Docker image (get_profile_base_image() against templates/bundles.yaml). Nothing else about a profile — its advertised package bundle, its advertised system-library bundle — is read by the Dockerfile generator. Those bundle definitions exist in bundles.yaml for documentation and for zzc list libs/zzc list pkgs, but generate_dockerfile_inline() does not consult them; actual R-package installation always comes from renv::restore() against renv.lock (or, in --no-renv mode, from DESCRIPTION), never from a profile’s declared package list.

Concretely, this means minimal’s advertised package bundle (renv, devtools, usethis, tinytest, roxygen2, here) is not actually installed by choosing the minimal profile — the only effect of minimal is the base image, rocker/r-ver. If your project’s code depends on packages the old base happened to provide, switching profile does not compensate by installing the new profile’s advertised bundle; it only changes the starting image.

Available Profiles

minimal (~650MB)

Base image: rocker/r-ver:latest. No tidyverse, no pandoc, no Quarto, no TeX Live baked in. Use for lightweight development, CI/CD, or any project that declares every dependency it needs in renv.lock/ DESCRIPTION rather than relying on anything the base image happens to ship.

tidyverse (~1.2GB) — the framework default

Base image: rocker/tidyverse:latest. Formerly named analysis as a profile; analysis is still accepted as a deprecated profile alias. Chosen as the framework’s default base image specifically because it is the only “full” rocker base (tidyverse/verse/rstudio/shiny) that also publishes an arm64 image — rocker/verse does not, and running it under QEMU emulation breaks pandoc outright.

rstudio (~980MB)

Base image: rocker/rstudio:latest. RStudio Server at http://localhost:8787 via make docker-rstudio.

publishing (~4.2GB)

Base image: rocker/verse:latest, which ships TeX Live and Quarto already baked in by rocker upstream (install_texlive.sh is run when rocker builds verse from tidyverse). Choosing this profile does not by itself set archetype or pdf — those are separate settings (see Section 5) that control whether the generator also installs anything on top of what rocker/verse already provides. In practice, because rocker/verse already has TeX Live, the TeX-install block in the generator is skipped on this profile regardless of pdf’s value; the only thing pdf/archetype still control on publishing is the LaTeX-package warm-up block (pre-baking the specific package closure your render needs, as root, at build time).

Specialized Environments via a Custom Base Image

Other environments are not separate named profiles. Build on a domain base image with --base/--base-image and add packages via renv:

zzc docker --base rocker/shiny
zzc docker --base bioconductor/bioconductor_docker
zzc docker --base rocker/geospatial

Profile Selection Guide

Research Domain Recommended Profile Alternative
General data analysis tidyverse minimal
Lightweight / CI minimal —
Interactive apps / RStudio IDE rstudio tidyverse
Manuscript / PDF rendering publishing tidyverse + pdf: true
Domain-specific (genomics, GIS, Shiny) tidyverse or minimal + custom --base —

The publishing vs. tidyverse + pdf: true choice is a real trade-off, not a stylistic one: publishing (4.2GB) ships the full rocker/verse TeX Live tree pre-installed; tidyverse + pdf: true (measured around 3.9GB for a project also running renv::restore()) installs only TeX Live on top of tidyverse, arrives at a somewhat smaller image, and — unlike publishing — has a native arm64 build. On Apple Silicon hardware, tidyverse + pdf: true is usually the better choice unless you specifically need something else rocker/verse provides.

Capability Settings: pdf and archetype

This section is a summary; docs/dockerfile-variable-reference.md Section 3 has the full mechanical walkthrough, including the precedence rules and the one asymmetry worth knowing about before you rely on it.

What archetype Controls

archetype (set via zzc init --archetype A, or persisted with zzc config set archetype A) primarily controls what zzc init scaffolds — which template files, which symlinks, which entry point a render targets. Six values exist: manuscript, book, blog, analysis (the default), package, simulation.

Only two of those six values feed into Dockerfile generation at all: manuscript and book default the project to needing a PDF toolchain; blog and book default it to needing Quarto. The other three (analysis, package, simulation) produce a Dockerfile identical to leaving archetype unset.

What pdf Controls

pdf is a direct, explicit override that always wins over the archetype-derived default:

  • pdf: true forces the TeX Live install block on (if the base image doesn’t already have TeX Live) and always also forces Quarto on.
  • pdf: false forces the TeX Live block off — even on a manuscript or book archetype.
  • Left unset, the archetype default from the table above applies.

There is no equivalent explicit setting for Quarto alone. The only ways to get Quarto installed are: set archetype to blog or book, or set pdf: true (which drags Quarto in as a side effect, with no way to decline it). A project wanting Quarto-only rendering, no PDF/TeX, outside the blog/book archetypes has no config key for that today.

Worked Decision

Ask these two questions, in order:

  1. Does the project render to PDF at all? If no, leave pdf unset and pick archetype: analysis (or package/simulation as fits) — you get neither TeX nor Quarto installed, the smallest image.
  2. If yes: does the base image already have TeX Live? Check with zzc list profiles — only publishing (rocker/verse) does. If you’re on any other profile, set pdf: true explicitly rather than relying on archetype alone, both so the setting survives a profile switch and so .zzcollab-state remembers it correctly across regeneration (zzc docker without --profile reuses the base image recorded in .zzcollab-state, and pdf’s remembered value in that same file is what keeps a bare zzc docker from silently dropping TeX from a manuscript project that never set CONFIG_PDF directly).

Two-Layer Package Management Architecture

Layer 1: Docker Profile (Team/Shared)

What: the base image’s own packages (and, for pdf/archetype-gated projects, TeX Live/Quarto). Control: --profile/--base at generation time. Shared: every build from the same Dockerfile gets the same image. Purpose: fast container startup, team consistency.

mkdir study && cd study
zzc tidyverse
zzc github
make docker-build
zzc dockerhub           # push for team members

Layer 2: Dynamic renv (Personal/Flexible)

What: packages installed inside the container with install.packages(), snapshotted to renv.lock automatically on exit via .Last() in .Rprofile. Control: whoever is working in the container, at any time. Purpose: analysis-specific packages, without rebuilding the image.

make r

install.packages("tidymodels")
q()   # exit R — snapshot to renv.lock happens automatically

# back on host
git add renv.lock DESCRIPTION
git commit -m "Add tidymodels"
git push

Key Principle: renv.lock is the Source of Truth for Packages

The Docker image provides the starting foundation and build-time performance; renv.lock is what actually pins exact package versions. A collaborator can, in principle, restore from renv.lock on top of a different compatible base image and get the same packages at the same versions — but see the caveat in “Docker Profile System” above: this only holds for packages that are genuinely recorded in renv.lock. Code that library()s a package the old base happened to ship, but that was never added to renv.lock/DESCRIPTION, is not actually reproducible across a profile switch, no matter how the renv layer is described in principle.

Practical Configuration Scenarios

Scenario 1: Solo Data Scientist 

zzc config init
zzc config set team-name "datasci"
zzc config set profile-name "tidyverse"

mkdir customer-churn && cd customer-churn
zzc tidyverse            # uses the configured defaults

Scenario 2: Team Lead Standardizing a Lab 

zzc config set team-name "psychlab"
zzc config set github-account "psychlab"

mkdir attention-study && cd attention-study
zzc tidyverse
zzc github

# Pin the project's profile and archetype explicitly so it survives
# regardless of what any individual team member's user config says
zzc config set-local profile-name "tidyverse"
zzc config set-local archetype "manuscript"
zzc config set-local pdf "true"

make docker-build
make docker-push-team
git add . && git commit -m "Team setup" && git push

Team members then only need:

zzc config set team-name "psychlab"
git clone https://github.com/psychlab/attention-study.git
cd attention-study
make docker-build        # ./zzcollab.yaml supplies the rest
make r

Scenario 3: Right-Sizing an Existing Project

A project on tidyverse + pdf: true wants to check whether a smaller base would work:

# Check what the code actually needs vs. what renv.lock actually pins
grep -rn "library(" analysis/ R/
grep -o '"[A-Za-z0-9.]*": {' renv.lock

# If everything the code uses is genuinely in renv.lock/DESCRIPTION:
zzc docker --profile minimal
zzc rebuild --verbose

# If the code relies on tidyverse packages absent from renv.lock, add
# them to renv.lock first (renv::snapshot() inside the container with
# those libraries loaded), or stay on the tidyverse profile.

See docs/dockerfile-variable-reference.md for exactly which variables this regeneration reads and in what order.

Configuration Validation and Troubleshooting

Validation Commands 

zzc config validate      # checks YAML syntax of user + project config
zzc config list          # merged configuration
zzc config list --local  # project config file's own content only

Common Issues

Issue 1: A setting isn’t taking effect

Project config always wins over user config for any key it sets. If zzc config get profile-name returns something other than what you set with zzc config set, check ./zzcollab.yaml for an override:

cat ./zzcollab.yaml
zzc config list --local

There is no built-in command that annotates which file supplied a merged value — comparing the two files directly is the only way.

Issue 2: ARM64 Mac Cannot Build an AMD64-Only Base Image 

Error: rocker/geospatial:latest: no matching manifest for linux/arm64/v8

Preferred fix: use an arm64-compatible base (tidyverse, rstudio, r-ver all publish arm64 images; rocker/verse does not) and add the domain packages via renv instead of switching base image.

Fallback: force amd64 under emulation (slower, but compatible):

export DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64
zzc docker --base rocker/geospatial

Issue 3: Missing User Configuration File 

Error: Configuration file not found: ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml
zzc config init

Issue 4: Docker Daemon Not Running 

docker info      # verify the daemon is reachable
# macOS/Windows: start Docker Desktop
# Linux: sudo systemctl start docker

Issue 5: TeX Live Build Failure on a Minimal Base

If zzc docker --profile minimal (or any profile lacking TeX Live) with pdf: true fails during the TeX Live install step with something like Package 'perl' has no installation candidate or Unable to locate package xzdec: this was a real bug in the generator (the apt package lists get cleared by the pandoc/Quarto steps that run immediately before the TeX Live block, and the bootstrap’s apt-get update was conditional on a check that missed that state). It is fixed as of the apt-get update being unconditional in that block; if you hit this on an older checkout, update the framework.

R Interface Configuration

The R interface wraps the same shell commands documented above; it does not add configuration capability the CLI lacks, and in one place (init_project()’s profile argument) it is currently narrower than the CLI: init_project() validates profile against only c("minimal", "analysis", "rstudio") — it does not currently accept "tidyverse" or "publishing" even though the shell CLI and bundles.yaml both support them. Use the shell CLI (zzc tidyverse, zzc publishing) directly if you need those profiles; init_project() will reject them.

library(zzcollab)

init_config()                               # create ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml
set_config("team_name", "myteam")
set_config("profile_name", "tidyverse")
set_config("github_account", "myusername")

team <- get_config("team_name")

all_config <- list_config()
print(all_config)

valid <- validate_config()
# init_project()'s profile argument accepts only "minimal", "analysis",
# or "rstudio" (narrower than the CLI; see note above)
init_project(
  team_name = "genomicslab",
  project_name = "cancer-study",
  profile = "analysis"
)

get_config_default(key, default) is the internal null-coalescing helper other package functions use; it is documented (?get_config_default) but is not typically called directly by users.

There are no get_effective_config(), get_config_sources(), or get_config_defaults() functions in the current R interface — an earlier version of this vignette described them; they do not exist in R/config.R. Source inspection (config list for the merged result, or the two YAML files directly for provenance) is the only way to answer “where did this value come from” today.

Best Practices

Configuration Strategy by Use Case

Solo Researcher

  • User configuration only.
  • Add packages via renv as needed; commit renv.lock, not user config.

Small Team (2–5 people)

  • Project configuration (./zzcollab.yaml), committed to Git, pins profile_name/archetype/pdf so every member’s regeneration produces the same Dockerfile regardless of their personal user config.
  • Team discusses package additions; renv tracks them.

Larger Organization

  • There is currently no system-wide config file to centralize this with (see Section 2 and Section 8) — distribute a project-config template or a shared zzcollab.yaml snippet instead.

Security Considerations

  • Never commit API keys, passwords, or credentials to zzcollab.yaml or renv.lock.
  • Use ~/.Renviron (outside Git) for secrets.
  • zzc github defaults to creating private repositories; confirm the visibility setting if that matters for your project.

Performance

  • minimal and tidyverse build fastest; publishing is the largest and slowest cold build (4.2GB, full TeX Live baked in by rocker).
  • A profile switch on an existing project (zzc docker --profile X) only changes the base image and regenerates the Dockerfile; it does not retroactively add the switched-to profile’s advertised packages — see the Layer 1 caveat above.
  • make check-renv (strict + auto-fix) and make snapshot (grow renv.lock/DESCRIPTION from the running image) are the two make targets to run before committing a package change.

Summary

Key Concepts

  1. Configuration hierarchy: project config overrides user config; there is no environment-variable layer for ordinary keys and no system-wide config file, despite documentation (and a dead constant in the source) once suggesting otherwise.
  2. Docker profiles: four built-in profiles resolving to a base image only (minimal, tidyverse, rstudio, publishing); a profile’s advertised package/library bundle is not installed by choosing it.
  3. Capability settings: pdf (explicit, tri-state, always wins) and archetype (supplies the default when pdf is unset) jointly gate the TeX Live and Quarto install blocks — see docs/dockerfile-variable-reference.md for the full logic.
  4. Two-layer package architecture: Docker image (shared) + renv (flexible), with renv.lock as the actual reproducibility source of truth — conditional on dependencies actually being declared there.
  5. R interface: thinner than the CLI in at least one place (init_project()’s profile set); prefer the CLI when in doubt.

Quick Reference 

# Initialize
zzc config init
zzc config set team-name "myteam"
zzc config set profile-name "tidyverse"

# Create a project
mkdir study && cd study
zzc tidyverse
zzc github

# Switch profile on an existing project
zzc docker --profile minimal
zzc rebuild --verbose

# Team collaboration
make docker-build && make docker-push-team     # lead
git clone ... && cd study && make docker-build # member

# Package management (inside container)
install.packages("package")
q()   # auto-snapshot on exit

# Before committing a dependency change
make snapshot
make check-renv

Changelog Note for Maintainers

This vignette was rewritten against the current shell implementation on 2026-10-19. Content removed from the prior version because it described behavior not present in the code:

  • A system-wide /etc/zzcollab/config.yaml configuration layer (ZZCOLLAB_CONFIG_SYSTEM is defined in lib/constants.sh but never read by load_config()).
  • A generic environment-variable configuration-override layer (ZZCOLLAB_TEAM_NAME and similar were never implemented).
  • config list --verbose and per-key source annotation in config list/config validate output.
  • Custom profile composition via a profiles: block in user config (base-image/libs-bundle/pkgs-bundle keys) — no code reads such a block.
  • The R functions get_effective_config(), get_config_sources(), get_config_defaults() (plural) — none exist in R/config.R.
  • The claim that the publishing profile is “capability-adaptive,” rendering PDF when a LaTeX toolchain is present and falling back to HTML otherwise by itself — no such fallback logic was found in modules/docker.sh; what exists is the pdf/archetype gating described in Section 5, which is an install-time decision, not a render-time fallback.

If any of the above is reintroduced in the codebase, this vignette should be updated to describe it again — these are accurate removals for this date’s source, not permanent judgments about the design.
